title: Grand Theft Auto 6 rumored to be launching on PC sooner than anyone expected, but I wouldn't get my hopes up too high
text:
A GamesBeat report claims that Grand Theft Auto 6—which still hasn't been announced for PC—will launch for PC sometime within the first three months of 2027. If correct, that means the game will drop, at most, just four months after its initial release on PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X/S consoles.
GamesBeat cites "four industry sources familiar with the studio's plans" in its report, all of whom requested anonymity. Rockstar has not yet commented on the claim.
It's a surprising claim. Earlier this year, we predicted that GTA 6 won't likely appear on PC before November 2027 , mainly because that's just how Rockstar rolls. We always have to wait.
The Unfortunate Timeline
Grand Theft Auto 3: 7 months between console and PC release
Vice City: 7 months
San Andreas: 8 months
Bully: 2 years
GTA 4: 7 months
Red Dead Redemption: 14 years, 5 months
GTA 5: 1 year, 6 months
RDR2: 1 year
Compared to that, a four month break between the console and PC releases, and possibly less, seems downright snappy, especially given how the gaps between GTA games themselves have grown over the decades.
Courtesy of Wikipedia :
(Image credit: Wikipedia) Not only would a Q1 release of GTA 6 on PC be an unusually brief break, it also puts the game in the midst of the post-holiday hangover, when we're all doing our best to nurse our bruised and battered bank balances back to health.
And that, I think, would feel especially egregious in the immediate aftermath of this year's holiday season, which for gamers will be driven by the release of GTA 6 on consoles. Rockstar loves the double dip , but punching the button again so soon after the console release would surely be viewed dimly by a not-insignificant number of people who would prefer the flexibility and power of the PC, but really don't want to wait for it.
Of course, if Rockstar or Take-Two confirms the GTA 6 PC release date really is that close—Take-Two's next quarterly financial report takes place on November 9, which might be a time for such a thing—some no doubt would wait for it, cannibalizing launch sales to some extent.
There's no shortage of people on social media saying they will indeed wait to buy GTA 6 if the PC version is indeed coming that quickly. That feeling may be even more widespread than it appears, given how much GTA 6 costs: At $100 for the premium edition and all the exclusive content it contains, you can understand why people might be more reticent about buying it multiple times than they were for earlier games in the series.
How about you?
Anything's possible, of course, and I would never presume to have a better understanding of these things than Strauss Zelnick and the rest of the GTA brain trust. But I also wouldn't bet on it—and for now I'm definitely taking all of this with a grain of salt. I've also reached out to Rockstar to ask about it, and will update if anyone answers.

title: World of Warcraft: Forever won't destroy what made the old classes so satisfying by modernizing them into oblivion: 'The level of mechanical complexity found in the beta classes is indicative of our intentions'
text:
Part of World of Warcraft: Forever's charm is that combat is considerably slower than the regular version of the MMO. It's the kind of game where you'll spend 38 seconds hitting a scorpion because there are so few buttons to press in the early stages of your journey.
Classes in WoW's past were simple, but had small quirks to them that you'd pick up over time. Melee classes, for example, can squeeze abilities in between their auto attacks to maximize their damage output. You'd never care about this if fights only took 10 seconds, like they do in WoW today, but back then you had to use all that time in more drawn-out battles for something .
The WoW: Forever beta has reminded me how satisfying it is to play a class that isn't built like Whac-A-Mole, where the challenge is to hit the right buttons the moment they start to glow. There's a rhythm to WoW's old classes and I'm delighted to hear that Blizzard fully intends to maintain it in WoW: Forever.
Blizzard developers told TechRadar that they want "to err on the side of simpler classes, but with engaging depth," and that all of it will align with its guiding principle of staying true to the old MMO's "core design, pacing, and tone."
"The level of mechanical complexity found in the beta classes is indicative of our intentions," Blizzard says.
That suggests to me that Blizzard isn't trying to speed up the pace of combat, nor will it look to shore up a class' weaknesses by adding new abilities where there were none before. My level 15 paladin will never graduate out of spending most of her time smacking monsters with a hammer while she waits for her Judgement ability to come back up. I won't ever have so many abilities on my bars that I'll need to refer to an infographic to understand which one to press first.
A strict adherence to the methodical combat of yore also means dungeons and raids will follow suit. Blizzard says encounter design will remain relatively simple so that some of the challenge will be found in preparing for them via gear sets, consumables, and team composition. I am skeptical that this will convince me to go back to farming for crafting items before every raid like I did as an over-achieving teen, but I can still appreciate that someone could take the time to do that again.
All of this makes me excited to see how creative the developers get with items that let WoW's old classes bend the rules a bit. Players have already discovered a sword for mages that deals bonus fire damage on frozen targets, for instance, which opens the door for more opportunities to play classes in ways you would've never seen in WoW's early days. My guess is this is what will ultimately drive players to stick around and make new secondary characters as part of Blizzard's goal to keep progression in WoW: Forever incremental and "horizontal".

title: Legendary level designer Richard 'Levelord' Gray has died
text:
Richard Gray, better known to gamers of a certain age as Levelord, has died. Gray's death was reported on social media by Apogee Entertainment, who paid tribute to his "legendary work on Duke Nukem 3D" and the lasting legacy he left behind.
We are deeply saddened by the passing of Richard “Levelord” Gray.From his legendary work on Duke Nukem 3D to the countless players and developers he inspired, Richard leaves behind a lasting legacy.Rest in peace, Levelord.
— @apogeeent.com ( @apogeeent.com.bsky.social ) 2026-10-13T20:34:18.004Z Gray worked as a level and map designer on numerous shooters in the late 1990s and early 2000, beginning with Duke Nukem 3D in 1996. Shortly after that game launched, he left 3D Realms and co-founded Hipnotic Interactive, later renamed to Ritual Entertainment, where he worked on games including Quake: Scourge of Armagon, Sin, Star Trek: Elite Force 2, Counter-Strike: Condition Zero, 25 to Life, and others.
He also earned a very specific fame for his "You're not supposed to be here" Easter egg in Duke Nukem 3D, which was only accessible via cheating.
Gray came to the game business at a (relatively, for the industry) advanced age. In a 2016 interview with Duke64Nukem.com he said he was 35 when he made his first Doom level, calling himself "a late bloomer with games," while Apogee founder Scott Miller said Gray was "in his 40s" when the studio hired him out of the Doom mod scene to work on Duke Nukem 3D.
(Image credit: Scott Miller (Twitter)) "I hired him to work on Duke 3D in 1994, after seeing some of his really impressive Doom levels—he was pretty active in the mod scene," Miller shared with PC Gamer. "He then moved to Dallas, and worked from our offices. He got along well with everyone and impressed everyone with his dedication and talent. Richard loved to push the engine to its limits and he came up with a lot of fun level design tricks, using portals for example, that our other level designers learned from.
"Richard was also so helpful to anyone who approached him for help getting into the industry or becoming a better designer. He had a terrific sense of humor, too. For example, in Duke 3D he made this hung jury room. A real legend."
(Image credit: Scott Miller/Apogee Entertainment) Other developers also paid tribute to Gray on social media:
Frederik Schreiber , Slipgate Ironworkers CEO: "Richard was, without a doubt, one of the kindest people I’ve ever met in the games industry. Incredibly humble, remarkably intelligent, endlessly creative, and always a pleasure to be around. Despite everything he had accomplished and the enormous influence his work had on my generation of game developers, he never carried himself as anything other than a genuinely good human being."
Richard B. Gray - LEVELORD11/15/1957 - 10/12/2026Just heard the news that an old friend of mine has passed on. Richard Gray - aka Levelord has departed the planet. I know he's dealt with cancer on and off for awhile now, a word that I cannot stand. Word comes from his wife Olga.
— @joesiegler.blog ( @joesiegler.blog.bsky.social ) 2026-10-13T20:34:18.129Z Andrew Hulshult , composer: "Richard Gray was one of those industry vets I always looked forward to hanging out with when I had the chance. He was VERY smart and I always felt like I learned something just from hanging out with him. I'm thankful Rob and Christine Atkins introduced me to him. R.I.P. friend."
Cliff Bleszinski , Gears of War creator: "RIP Richard 'Levelord' Gray. You broke the mold, fella. Guy paved the way for so many level/environment designers."
Devastating news today. Richard “Levelord” Gray was such a great guy. Like many of our friends, I wish I could have hung out with him again. He was full of life, a gentle soul, and an excellent level designer. He was called “Levelord” for a reason.
— @johnromero.bsky.social ( @johnromero.bsky.social.bsky.social ) 2026-10-13T20:34:17.887Z I loved the first episode of DN3D but was more drawn in by E2 and E3 that had such distinctive designs. We’re gonna miss you, man. You were one of the best.
— @johnromero.bsky.social ( @johnromero.bsky.social.bsky.social ) 2026-10-13T20:34:18.264Z Siegler said Gray had struggled with cancer "on and off for a while now." but the cause of death was not announced. He was 68.

title: Kojima says he was 'just like Bryan' from the Resident Evil movie when he played RE1 in 1996: 'I kept getting game over after game over, shouting F***!'
text:
Zach Cregger's Resident Evil film was released to critical acclaim last month, with more than one reviewer calling it ' the best videogame movie ever .' Another review dropped today, from none other than Hideo Kojima, and it's (seemingly) a glowing one.
"I wasn’t particularly interested at first, but since it’s Zach Cregger’s latest film, I went to see Resident Evil," Kojima posted on Twitter on October 12.
"Right from the opening, it hits you with music reminiscent of "The Thing." From there, it’s a relentless barrage of classic horror techniques, terrifying situations, and jump scares that never lets up until the very end."
That bit is sorta why I said seemingly above. Do I detect a little backhanded praise? Calling it a "relentless barrage" isn't necessarily a compliment, saying a director used "classic horror techniques" could be a way of saying it's unoriginal, and pointing out that there are "jump scares" throughout might suggest it's not a particularly sophisticated film.
Or, maybe I'm coloring Kojima's statements with my own paranoia which endlessly scans any compliment I'm given for potential criticism. You be the judge.
Anyway, here's the real meat of Kojima's little review:
"This isn’t a film adaptation of Resident Evil. It’s a film about the experience of playing Resident Evil, controller in hand," Kojima continued. "It reminded me of how I felt when I first played the original Resident Evil on PlayStation back in 1996. I was just like Bryan in this movie. I kept getting game over after game over, shouting 'F***!' over and over again. lol"
Preach. The movie was so much fun because it really did feel like you were watching someone play the game, as Bryan dealt with the horrors he faced the same way we all do in a Resi game: by screaming, running, and often demonstrating terrible aim. As Elie observed, the Resident Evil movie is the best because Bryan sucks .
I've embedded Koj's tweet below, and you should check it out because it includes a picture of the Japanese poster for the Resident Evil movie. It's rad.

title: Rockstar co-founder Dan Houser says he 'failed' with Max Payne 3, and I'm sorry Danno but that's just plain wrong
text:
Dan Houser is a co-founder of Rockstar Games and so I would never presume to tell him he's wrong about any of the games Rockstar has made— except in this one particular instance, where I feel obligated to step up and say, 'Dan, I'm sorry bud, but you're wrong.'
The game in question is Max Payne 3 , on which Houser played a central role, and one he seems rather down on: In an interview with IGN , he said the game was a "failure" because, simply put, he's not Sam Lake, the Remedy creative director who wrote the first two Max Payne games.
As a very linear game, Max Payne 3 "was a little different" from the open world GTA games he was accustomed to, Houser said, but he also really enjoyed the experience. "I loved what we did design-wise, the way the game didn't have loads, the way it felt like a 12-hour movie, some of the visual stuff we did with words on screen.
Alas, he continued, "I felt we were creating a really cool digital noir experience, and the consensus at the time was that people hated it.
"So I got that completely wrong," Houser said. "I know Sam Lake well, and he's a very good guy and really talented. I thought we'd done a good job of doing another Max Payne game. Some people liked it; lots didn't. So we got it wrong, or I got it wrong. I failed. My bit was not a success.
"The game is beautifully made, and it wasn't as successful as it should have been. So I would say a large amount of that failure was on me as one of the people making the decisions and also as the writer, when people really missed his writing."
Max Payne 3 is a really interesting case study because it's very much a Max Payne game—grim and gritty, filled with bullet time, body drops, and snappy commentary about how much life sucks—but it's also a full-on Rockstar game, and thus a very different vibe from the previous two entries in the series. Fans who were expecting more of the same—or insisting on it, really—were bound to be disappointed.
But Max Payne 3 itself is nothing short of a brilliant, powerhouse cinematic shooter. It really does feel like "a 12-hour movie," powered by lush cut scenes, a brilliant soundtrack by industrial rock group Health, and great performances across the board, in particular from James McCaffrey in the title role.
With all due respect to Remedy, this is where McCaffrey really hit his stride, digging deep to deliver some truly great lines:
I wouldn't know right from wrong if one of them was helping the poor and the other was banging my sister.
Look at me, I'm standing in a nightclub, listening to music I can't stand, I'm five thousand miles from home, I'm armed, and I'm drinking. You don't want to listen to advice from me, amigo.
I had a hole in my second favourite drinking arm, and the only way we were likely to get Fabiana back now was in instalments.
I'd killed more cops than cholesterol and still no sign of Becker. It wasn't the first time it dawned on me I should probably have gone over the plan in more detail, but it was too late for that now.
I was a dumb American in a place where dumb Americans are less popular than the clap.
I'd put a big shit-eating grin on my face and let these assholes take turns trying to kill me. That's my style and it's too late in the day to hope for change.
We'd half destroyed Sao Paulo's most hallowed place of worship. Looking back it was strange how the cops never showed up. But things had a habit of only making sense to me looking back, long after I'd run out of time to fix them.
I'd been sitting at the bar for three hours, or about five years, depending on how you looked at things. I tried not to look at things.
It is fair to say that Max Payne 3 wasn't a massive commercial success: In 2012, publisher Take-Two Interactive said sales of the game came in " lower than expected ," resulting in a significantly increased net loss for the quarter. But that's hardly the only measure of success, and I think it's notable that Take-Two said the same, at the same time, about Spec Ops: The Line , a game widely heralded, then and now, for its daring, subversive narrative.
Max Payne 3 was a slower burn, but I think the passage of time has given us a far better perspective on what Rockstar actually delivered: As former PC Gamer writer Andy Kelly wrote a full decade ago, "Over the years I’ve developed a greater appreciation for the risks Rockstar took in breaking Remedy’s established, and beloved, mould."
"It’s a radical departure, but it works," the other Andy wrote in his very correct take on Max Payne 3 . "It’s always interesting to see a familiar character thrust into an unfamiliar situation, and Max is hilariously out of place in Brazil. As if being a white American in a favela didn’t draw enough unwanted attention, he makes his life even more difficult by wearing the loudest Hawaiian shirt imaginable. He was comfortable in New York, but here he’s an outsider, and the game plays up to it brilliantly."
And so, Dan, with all due respect, I have to say, 'I'm sorry bud, but you're wrong.' Max Payne 3 may have been divisive in its time, and it may not have been the big hit you were hoping for, but I sure wouldn't call it a failure. I'd say Rockstar, and you, absolutely nailed it.

title: Valve is clearing out its discontinued Index VR headsets if you want a cheap piece of history
text:
With the recently launched Steam Frame superseding the Index VR headset, Valve has heavily discounted remaining stock of the latter. The Index VR headset launched in 2019 for $499, but now you can get one for $399.20.
Keep in mind that the Index VR headset doesn't come with controllers or a base station. A package bundling those used to cost $999, but that option is no longer available and thus, there's no associated discount.
Left controller replacements and replacement tethers are going for $119.20 and $103.20 respectively. No, there aren't any right controller replacements listed. It seems that if you want controllers for your Index VR, you'll probably need to buy them elsewhere. The same goes for base stations.
"Valve Index is no longer being produced," reads a Steam news item published earlier today. "Remaining Index headsets, controllers, and accessories are still available at the new prices below while supplies last."
That "while supplies last" is crucial: obviously Valve won't be making any more, and they've given no sense of how many they have lying around. If you really want one, perhaps as a collectible, I'd probably act fast.
Valve designer Lawrence Yang indicated that Index VR was no longer being manufactured last year, but this is the first official word from Valve on the matter.
The Index was a tidy piece of kit when it launched in April 2019. Our review called it the best VR headset available, while falling short of a 2.0 approach to VR. Nowadays the thought of being tethered to a PC while using VR is a bit dated, but back then it was still the norm despite the original Meta Quest—then known as Oculus Quest—popularising cord-free VR a few months later.

title: Steam now has a maddening bouncing logo screensaver, and I'm pretty sure it doesn't perfectly hit the corners
text:
The Steam client got a major new update today, with Big Picture Mode receiving the brunt of the attention. Most exciting, I guess, is that the previously beta-only screensaver feature for Big Picture Mode is now live for the general public. In its default mode the screensaver will display art from recently played games, as well as any recent screenshots you've taken. But you can add your own custom screensavers too, which is nice.
Valve also has "a retro inspired bouncing logo screensaver" which you can select in the new dropdown menu found under Settings / Customization. As the name implies, the Steam logo bounces around a black screen, changing color every time it hits an edge. Valve has not made this screensaver the default screensaver, and it's lucky that it didn't: it's a work of diabolical cruelty. It will drive you to despair.
The screensaver references the ye olde screensaver built into DVD players in the late '90s and early '00s. If you're too young to remember it firsthand you've probably heard of it: a DVD Video logo bounces around a black screen, changing color every time it hits an edge. This unassuming but actually-quite-psychologically-damaging display has gone viral several times over the last decade or so, to the extent that, if you Google it, the Google logo will bounce around the search results page. It even has a Wikipedia page .
Why? Everyone subjected to it in the pre-social media era seems to have experienced the same intense desire for that DVD Video logo to perfectly hit the corner of the television's display. And how often does that happen? Extremely rarely.
If you don't know what I'm talking about, it's essential that you watch this ten hour video of the DVD Video screensaver:
People say smartphone screens are ruining our lives, undermining our attention, destroying literacy etcetera, and I mostly agree. But at least they've saved us from the hypnotic tyranny of the goddamned bouncing DVD logo screensaver. Screw that thing.
Anyway, Valve has its own version now, and after watching it—mostly against my will—for about half-an-hour while I ate my lunch, I'm pretty sure this abhorrent thing never pays out with a perfect corner-hitting moment.
My suggestion? Don't even think about it. Don't even turn it on as a joke. You may never re-emerge.
Back on topic, though, this Steam client update is genuinely huge compared to the norm. Startup performance has been "improved" to some unspecified degree, for example. A new experimental video codec, Pyrowave, has been added to Remote Play which apparently "allows high bandwidth, low latency video streaming". Linux users get a whole bunch of tweaks and fixes too. But the focus is very much on minor improvements to Big Picture Mode, which is good news for Steam Machine and Deck users.
The update notes in their voluminous glory are here . And I repeat: don't go near the bouncing logo screensaver.

title: I just tricked DLSS into running on my AMD GPU in Cyberpunk 2077 and Alan Wake 2 and all it took was running a single script
text:
If you have an older AMD card, you might want to take a look at a new, easy-to-use tool that allows you to use DLSS rather than FSR 3. I've been trying it out, and it works really well and is easy to install.
The tool, HelixSR , works by making patched games believe they're still running FSR 3.1, but it replaces the upscaling algorithm with DLSS 3.7 (Model E). It bases the new upscaling DLL file it hands the game on the official DLSS one. The upscaling is done using your regular shader cores, of course, given there aren't Tensor cores to make use of in your AMD GPU.
This being said, the differences in image quality are very far from night and day, and dropping in the DLSS patch actually decreases performance very slightly.
I'd still say the tool is worth a try. If worst comes to worst, you can uninstall it by running a simple pre-packaged script.
AMD has come a long way since the time when its upscaling solution was far behind Nvidia's, both in terms of game support and quality. Now, so many games support FSR 4 that I can't justify taking the time to count them like I used to when I wrote about it, and image quality isn't too far behind Nvidia.
But much of this depends on which version of each side's tech you're comparing. FSR 4 is supported only on the latest RX 9000-series or 7000-series cards, so RDNA 1 and RDNA 2 cards (RX 5000-series and RX 6000-series, respectively) have to stick to FSR 3. It's these cards that I think will primarily benefit, here.
The primary benefit will be for older AMD GPUs that can't use FSR 4. And if you notice a bigger difference in image quality than I do between FSR 3 and DLSS Model E, that's a nice bonus.
How to install
Installation is very easy. Unless you want to try the latest, experimental version, you can download the 1.8.1 zip (under Assets) and extract it to a safe place such as your root C:\ drive. Then, run the batch file and let it do its work.
It'll ask you which games you want it running on, and that's it. Just hit Enter for the ones you want to try it on, or input 'n' for those you don't, and the script will handle the rest.
Pay attention to the final run of text before the script closes, as this tells you what to select in-game—in Cyberpunk and Alan Wake 2 using my RX 9070 XT, that was FSR or FSR 3. And if you want to uninstall it, just run the uninstall batch script.
Image quality
For my part, the difference seemed slight but not invisible. Here's how some far-away metal stairs look in Cyberpunk:

Upscaling comparison in Cyberpunk 2077

title: '123456' password was all a hacker reportedly needed to expose over 8 million people's personal data
text:
Please, please, please do not use '123456' as any kind of password. I know that may seem obvious, but apparently it bears repeating if a recent hack of Denmark's Central Register of Persons (CPR) is anything to go by.
To recap, the CPR administration said earlier this month that it had become aware of a breach that took place in September (PDF warning). This exposed personal details—names, addresses, ID numbers—of 8.8 million people, both living and deceased. It was confirmed at the time that the legitimate access of a private Danish firm had been exploited by the attacker.
A person claiming responsibility for the attack has come forward this week. Not only that, they say that they gained access to the CPR via an account which had the password '123456'. According to Danish newspaper Politiken , this was one of three accounts held by the private firm with that same password. One of these was an administrator account. Talk about a cybersecurity boo-boo.
The self-identified attacker claims they have no intention of leaking or selling the data they lifted, so that's something. Still, we're left with the uncomfortable reminder that those who should know better don't always have the best password management.
The Danish firm at the heart of this attack has been identified as Pays ApS. This company was granted access to the CPR in order to provide various services, like validating business customers' records.
(Image credit: Chris Ratcliffe/Bloomberg via Getty Images) The self-identified attacker gained access to the Pays ApS account on September 10, and then ran 14 million automated searches of the CPR between then and September 20 . The attack was only discovered on October 2 when an employee at the Ministry of Research, Education and Digitalisation noticed an unusually high invoice, which indicated that many more searches than the norm were being made by Pays ApS.
Hackers are all too aware of the most common passwords, with ' 123456' often bafflingly popular among them . Bottom line, now might be a good time to update your passwords to something uniquely yours or to otherwise investigate password tools (though not even something like a password manager is completely air tight ).
Not every hacker is rocking a password cracking rig with 12 Nvidia GeForce RTX 5090s —for instance, I was particularly charmed by the password-cracking Game Boy Advance that is ' about thirty million times slower than a modern cracking rig '. But if your password is '123456', a hacker won't need hardware any more dedicated than their brain to crack open your account like a coconut.

title: OpenAI employee arrested for allegedly using AI and toilet paper to record confidential meetings - FBI director Kash Patel jumps at the chance to say AI companies are 'essential' for national security
text:
An OpenAI engineer has been arrested and charged for using (or endeavoring to use) an audio recording device to spy on confidential company communications. That's according to the US Department of Justice , and while commercial espionage is nothing new, there's a certain sardonic twist to this one: it seems the accused employee did so with the help of AI. Oh, and some toilet paper.
According to FBI director Kash Patel's summary of the complaint, Saudi Arabian national Abdulrahman Alfozan "allegedly concealed a covert recording device inside his employer’s executive conference room to secretly capture sensitive communications about the company’s super intelligence technology."
In case you hadn't heard, that's what the US bigwigs are calling AI now: superintelligence. Courtesy of President Trump, of course, who said last month that the Administration will use this term in place of artificial intelligence "in any applicable setting."
The FBI director also said, "Protecting American SI innovation is essential to safeguarding our nation’s economic strength and national security, and the FBI views that mission as one of our highest counterintelligence priorities."
The complaint says that Alfozan had worked for OpenAI since July 2025 as an engineer, and at the end of last month OpenAI discovered a USB audio recording device plugged into a conference room TV. According to the Justice Department, the device, which had been installed for a couple of days before discovery, was "concealed in toilet paper."
The complaint also alleges that Alfozans' spouse's "chatbot" account (no mention of whether that's a ChatGPT account or something else) submitted prompts related to things such as "build[ing] a continuous audio recorder", "improv[ing] audio and live listening", and "encrypt[ing] the SD card." There were allegedly also prompts relating to the specific recording device that was found.
(Image credit: Getty Images) The conference room in question seems to have been an important one. The Department of Justice explains:
"According to the complaint, meetings in the executive conference room where Recording Device 1 was discovered frequently involved discussions of highly confidential technical, commercial, and strategic information, including proprietary research, product plans, and business-development opportunities, as well as nonpublic information about Open AI’s technical progress and strategic decisions, capabilities, priorities, government engagements, and commercial relationships."
Various appendages of the state seem to be taking this very seriously. Which isn't surprising, of course, given AI development—no, I'm not calling it 'SI'—is deemed important to national security and prosperity.
(Image credit: Urbazon via Getty Images) Director of National Intelligence Jay Clayton said: "This serious situation underscores why winning the global super intelligence race is a national security prerogative... The intelligence community remains committed to safeguarding America’s cutting-edge intellectual property from foreign threats."
US Attorney Craig H. Missakian for the Northern District of California seems to agree: "For us it is a matter of national security. This arrest highlights our relentless efforts in partnership with the FBI to identify and prosecute those who seek to steal our technology, as alleged in the complaint."
My question, however, is this: If the allegations are true, would Alfozan have been able to do this without the use of an AI chatbot? Snakes and tails, and all that.

title: GTA 6 was delayed partially because the amount of NPCs was 'horrifying' and required a dedicated studio full of writers to handle
text:
Grand Theft Auto 6 , originally slated to be released back in May, was delayed to November —the reason given at the time was "to finish the game with the level of polish you have come to expect and deserve". And while that still very much holds true, the reality of the game's scope and stature was apparently kinda terrifying from a production standpoint.
Speaking with Bloomberg , co-head of development Rob Nelson commented on one reason for the delay—the amount of NPCs that were required to populate Leonida: "The projections they were giving us were horrifying." The solution? A kind of NPC emergency room, an entire studio set up in LA solely designed to handle the workload.
Another development co-head, Phil Hooker, comments: "I think when it became apparent that some areas weren’t going to make it, that’s when we decided to make the shift of date. We could hit that schedule, but it won’t be the game we want to make."
Being perfectly candid, for a moment: This fills me both with a sense of dread and relief. The former is acquired from the same residual existential fear I felt back in May of last year. Namely, the fact that videogames probably aren't meant to look this pretty or be this sprawling—that the industry simply cannot support them, and that GTA 6 is going to be the last of its kind.
The relief comes from the fact that, in an industry culture seemingly determined to figure out how to push creatives out of their seats as quickly as possible with AI ? That a bunch of actual writers and producers were brought in to handle the load. There's this perception that background details in video games can be automated because, well, they're background details—they're not important, surely?
But in my humble opinion, those are, in fact, the details you want to get right. The background chatter and worldbuilding of a game is important because it'll lend said game its texture, even if you're just parodying Florida.
GTA 6 will be a better game because, when its developers panicked, Rockstar (which doesn't have the brightest industry track record , let's be clear) didn't cheap out on the massive writing load it'd accidentally saddled itself with, and that's commendable in a vacuum.
Now, is it healthy or normal that an industry giant can be so large it can pop-up an entire studio in LA full of writers just to handle a temporary task? Probably not, and it's certainly not something that's gonna last, particularly not at the industry's current price-point .

title: Arc Raiders' PvE test is finally here and it's the perfect reason to jump back in
text:
God, life is stressful. There's too much to do and too few hours in the day to do it. So when I get a couple of hours of free time in the evening I have to be pretty mindful of what I do, and let me tell you getting domed in Arc Raiders by some rando hiding in a bush is not at the top of my list.
It's a shame, because I love the world of Arc Raiders. I love its mystery, its grandiose landscapes, and its bizarre communal storytelling that you just can't get in most games. But there's finally a solution: the PvE test.
(Image credit: Embark Studios) Embark teased the test a few weeks ago, finally admitting that due to a large portion of its audience favouring a more passive approach to the game, it would test out a temporary PvE toggle . While Frozen Trail released a few days ago, the PvE test has only gone live now, and it's a hell of a lot of fun.
Dropping into Pendola Pass has never been so chill, well, it's more chill than usual; as soon as I came out of my bunker I was met with hellfire raining down on me and the pinging of bullets as they shot past my face while a couple of players attempted to take down the newer arc, a Bully. 'Ok' I thought to myself, 'I guess I'll start here'.
The Bully isn't anywhere near as lethal as a Queen but it's tankier than I expected it to be for its size as it ate my Wolfpack grenade like it was nothing. I hadn't come equipped for a fight like this but thanks to the growing group of curious raiders we managed to take it down before long. It may sound boring to someone who loves the adrenaline dump of PvP, but for someone who just wants to explore the map, take down arcs, and perhaps help out their fellow raider along the way this experience right here is golden.
(Image credit: Embark Studios) Instead of shuffling around bushes and hiding in the shadows I feel relatively free to wander about the surface and actually take in the surrounding views. You still have to be careful of arcs, but not having your blood run cold when you hear footsteps closing in to your location is such a welcome change.
In fact, it's quite the opposite now, hearing raiders close by reassures me that if things were to go wrong, someone would help—which is especially nice when arcs in the PvE mode will finish you off if they catch you moving while downed. After taking out a number of arcs on my way to the Observatory my hubris was bolstered, so when I saw the new Skulker, a seemingly small and insignificant enemy, I thought that it would be easy pickings. I was wrong.
(Image credit: Embark Studios) Maybe I was just unlucky, but this Skulker had a couple of other friends with it, and it took way more ammo than I thought to take it down. I was pinned behind a couple of crates, quickly going through all my reserves and trying to come up with an exit strategy when I heard gunfire. I have no idea where it came from, perhaps it was an angel from above, but a stranger saw I was in need of assistance, helped take the Skulkers out, and then moved on.
They were gone before I could say thank you, so I decided to pay it forward instead. On my way to the extract I saw a bunch of arcs swarming an outbuilding, I didn't have much ammo left but I still wanted to help, so help I did. I started taking pot shots at some of the Wasps to distract them away from the shed and before long another raider popped their head out and together we took them out. Nothing was said, but after a thankful wave we went our separate ways and I extracted back to Speranza.
As I said before, I love Arc Raiders for its world, action, and crafting, but it also just feels really nice to help without the worry that the person you've just saved may shoot you in the back of the head and ruin any faith in humanity you had left. The PvE test is a welcome change of pace, and I'll be playing it almost exclusively while I still have the chance.

title: Epic says its new 'vibe coded' Epic Games Store launcher is faster than Steam
text:
The big Epic Games Store rebuild teased earlier this year has arrived as a new "preview" client available to download for Windows and Mac, as well as Linux for the first time.
PC Gamer was shown a demonstration of the client in advance of the announcement, and the speed improvement appeared significant. Epic claims that it's halved the launcher's startup time, and that it now goes from a cold start to the store page 46% faster than Steam. (Epic says its technical improvements have been verified by an external vendor. We have yet to test the client ourselves.)
There are also updates to the interface: A redesigned library view is the standout change, and it includes the option to bring in shortcuts to games installed with Steam and other clients.
In a blog post , Epic refers to the new client as "vibe coded," a term for prompting AI tools to produce code. The term be taken as either derogatory or endearing depending on who's talking.
Epic goes for laughs, saying that it opted to use AI because "programming is hard," but the company isn't joking about its use of AI coding tools. On a call this week with Epic Games Store GM Martin Keely, who took over for the outgoing Steve Allison in August, I asked whether AI was used primarily to analyze the existing EGS code for opportunities to improve it, or to write new code. He affirmed it was the latter.
"We started from scratch," said Keely. "This is a completely new architecture for both the store and the launcher shell. So we did look at functionality that existed and said we want to replicate that, but not the code itself. So [AI] was a tool to write and review new features and new capabilities from the ground up in a different tech stack than what we had previously."
Epic says its new client launches 46% faster than Steam. (Image credit: Epic Games) You'd be hard pressed to find any big games company that isn't mucking about with AI, but Epic is particularly bullish on the tech, and willing to confront public disapproval. On Monday, Bloomberg reported that Epic instructed the team working on an unannounced Star Wars and Marvel shooter to take an "AI first" approach to development.
"We have a huge pivot underway here at Epic, moving developers around to retool for maximum AI acceleration," Epic CEO Tim Sweeney said after that news was reported. "The aim isn't to do the same stuff with fewer people, but to enable everyone here to build MORE and BETTER stuff, and to bring the benefits to all teams using Unreal."
The use of "vibe coded" to describe this new client, which is sure to draw some eyerolls, seems to me like a clear statement from Epic that it is unbothered by AI critics.
For now, the release of the new client is not being communicated through the existing Epic Games Store software. Epic is treating it like a beta test, expecting gradual adoption through word-of-mouth while it addresses feedback.
The preview client can be downloaded at launcher.epicgames.com , and alongside the expected Windows and macOS versions, there's also a Linux build.
In conjunction with that news, Epic announced that it's working on upgrading Easy Anti-Cheat so that it can bring Fortnite to Linux and help other multiplayer games make the jump.

title: Fortnite is coming to Linux once Epic improves Easy Anti-Cheat
text:
Epic intends to launch Fortnite on Linux, but first, it's "rebuilding Easy Anti-Cheat" to support the move.
"Once [EAC Linux v2 is] working with a critical mass of distro maintainers, we'll bring Fortnite to Linux via the Epic Games Launcher," the company announced. "We'll also make these improvements available to other developers so they can bring their games to Linux players."
More PC games than ever are playable on Linux, thanks in part to Valve's Proton emulation, which allows many Windows games to be played on SteamOS and has been essential to the Steam Deck's success. But some of the biggest multiplayer games have been holdouts, because opening the doors to Linux represents a security and cheating risk.
For example, former Facepunch COO Alistair McFarlane said last year that the studio's popular survival game, Rust, was unsupported on Linux because of cheating.
"There are no plans to support Proton or Linux," McFarlane said at the time. "It's a vector for cheat developers, and one that would be poorly maintained by both us and EAC due to the low user base. When we stopped support for Linux, we saw more cheat users exploiting Linux, than actual legitimate users."
Epic's move could potentially change that calculation for Rust and other games.
One hurdle: Most of the people I know who play games on Linux do so on a Steam Deck, but according to an Epic blog post that goes into the plan's technical details, the Steam Deck does not currently support the new EAC Linux v2 solution. Epic says that it is "actively talking with Valve" about making it happen.
Regarding Fortnite specifically, game security engineering director Rick Deist told PC Gamer on a call this week that Epic is "investigating compatibility with Steam Deck and SteamOS devices." (In related news, Epic has released a new Epic Games Store client which includes a Linux version for the first time.)
"We want to let players play where they want to play as much as possible," said Deist.

title: Doom can 'run' on a DNS database now, and one of the technology's pioneers says 'I can't decide whether this is deliciously horrible, or else horribly delicious'
text:
In the early 2000's, the perennial question was whether a powerful system could run Crysis. These days, it's whether a minimal one can run Doom. We've seen an affirmative answer to this question when it comes to vapes , a motherboard BIOS , and even a pregnancy test . And now? A DNS database.
To be clear, we've seen Doom broken down into DNS text records before , but this time it seems like the database is doing more than file storage. This new version is courtesy of Corey Quinn over at The Register , who explains: "I have compiled Doom for a 32-bit machine whose arithmetic and memory live in DNS."
DNS, for those unaware, means ' domain name system ', and is the system that translates URLs into IP addresses that computers can actually interact with to visit. You can also create your own DNS databases with your own entries.
Quinn realised that such a database could be used essentially as a "librarian", pulling pre-made answers to relevant operations: "The database itself is 6.4 million rows of truth tables."
One of the main pioneers of DNS, Paul Vixie, said : "I can't decide whether this is deliciously horrible, or else horribly delicious. in either case, it's the best use of RFC 2136 DNS UPDATE that I've ever seen."
DNS UPDATE is what allows DNS records to be changed, which is also what's required for values and variables to change and be updated in a game world. That's the key trick here, as far as I can tell: Quinn realised there's enough similarity in the way DNS works to essentially replicate the usual conditional 'if this, then this' way that code works.
(Image credit: id Software) "I want to be very clear here: this isn't DNS pretending to be a CPU." says Quinn. "The instruction decoding is done ahead of time by a compiler; BIND never executes an instruction itself. All that it sees is a key-value read, a conditional write, and 6.4 million rows of precomputed answers.
"It's not really a computer; it's simply a very good database. And that turns out to be enough."
Yes, that's right: 6.4 million rows. And it's hardly a snappy experience, as one update takes just over 54 seconds: "Doom says its tic rate is 35 per second, so 'playable' is a tic every 28.6 ms. I remain at 54,000 ms, which is three orders of magnitude away from victory."
So, not exactly a practical gaming experience, but certainly a fun project. If you want to try it out, Quinn has published the code on GitHub , so have at it.

title: If New Blood had made Dusk 2, there'd be no Iron Lung, 'and now David Szymanski has got a movie that made $50 million'—so maybe there's wisdom in not churning out sequels
text:
New Blood boss Dave Oshry isn't interested in running a massive studio that follows the blockbuster strategy of milking its successful games for all they're worth. The publisher-developer combo has enjoyed a string of big wins with its boomer shooters, but Oshry's plan for building on success is to invest that money into new projects.
"I think a lot of studios would have a big hit like Ultrakill ," Oshry tells us, "and then they would maybe open a big office, or just milk the shit out of Ultrakill and do Ultrakill spinoffs, or use that money to make sequels. And I've decided to put that money into projects like Gloomwood and Fallen Aces , artsy projects like Tenebris Somnia . That’s what I've decided to do with our success because I can, because we're independent."
The goal, says Oshry, has never been to create "a big studio with an office and hundreds of employees … I don't know why anyone would want that". And thankfully he doesn't have to deal with shareholders and investors telling him to just keep milking and keep growing.
"The fact that we're one studio and that I control everything means that I can make those kinds of decisions," he says. "If we had publishers or shareholders or investors, they would be like, ‘No, you need to take that money and reinvest it into things that are going to make more money so we can get bigger returns.’ They would be like, ‘You need to be working on Ultrakill spinoff games. You need to be working on Dusk 2, Faith: Chapter Four. Why haven't you made a survival crafting game out of this yet? You need to be reinvesting in the IPs and making money, money, money.’ And we're just like, ‘What cool thing do we want to do? What's coming down the pipe?’"
This isn't to say that New Blood doesn't support its games or give players another taste of the things that they dig. Dusk and Amid Evil continue to be updated, and there have been conversations about a new episode for Dusk or even a proper sequel. A Dusk spin-off is in the works, too, called Dungeons of Dusk , though it's from a different developer, not David Szymanski.
It's all about IP, it always has been with AAA.
Dave Oshry
But this is still a far cry from the big publisher strategy of making IPs and bleeding them dry. Like Ubisoft, for example. "Look at fucking Heroes of Might and Magic," says Oshry. "Look at what's happened to that bloody series over the years. Everybody loves Heroes 3, and that was a million years ago. Ubisoft has whored that IP out all over the place for decades, and now finally you've got someone like Hooded Horse making something like Olden Era, and people are like, ‘Yeah, good, this is what we wanted’. But it's all about IP, it always has been with AAA."
Oshry offers Wolverine as another example. "It became designed by corporate, and look what happened. I don't think it was the game they originally set out to make, but it was the game they had to ship. At New Blood we’re never putting out games because it's a game we had to ship—because we had to meet a deadline or we had investors or shareholders. We're literally just trying to make the best games we can and make as many people happy as we can."
If New Blood followed the received wisdom that Sony or Ubisoft follow, it likely wouldn't be the success that it is. "If I just forced David to make Dusk 2," Oshry says, "we never would have gotten Iron Lung . Iron Lung, Markiplier, $50 million [box office] never would have happened if I made David do Dusk 2. And now David Szymanski has got a movie that made $50 million, funded by a YouTuber. That doesn't happen if I don't run New Blood the way that I do. It works. It works for us."
Looking at the state of the industry, the failure of big games like Wolverine, the so-called 'Xbox reset', the grotesque layoffs, it certainly looks like blockbuster game development, endless sequels and an obsession with IP is unsustainable.
"As we've seen with all the layoffs, developers are disposable, whether you make a hit game or not," Oshry says. "What is a hit? Your game can sell millions of copies, but it doesn't balance the balance sheet. So everybody gets laid off. Imagine working for six years on a game, it's not the game you wanted to make anyway, and then you get laid off because it's not the game that sells. And you're like, ‘Well, maybe it would have been if it was the game we wanted to make, and not the game that had to ship, like a Wolverine.’
"People are always like, ‘Oh, the industry is dying and imploding’. We're doing fine. I guess we're the lucky ones. But I think we made our own luck by making the kind of games we want to make, and knowing that they'll sell to the kind of people who like our games."

title: Looks like a lighter, carbon fibre version of the best gaming mouse I've held is on its way, but don't look at the price tag
text:
The Razer Viper V4 Pro is the single best mouse I've laid my sweaty fingertips on, and I've laid them on a fair few. It's sleek, light, has tons of battery life, a comfy shape, and is incredibly well-built. So you can probably understand my excitement to hear that there might be a new, lighter, carbon fiber version just around the corner.
That's according to peripheral reviewer iitzKami , who has posted on X saying that "Razer is going carbon fibre." The reviewer includes some images, too, which do look legit, though it's always difficult to be sure these days.
There'll apparently be a CF version of the DeathAdder V4 Pro , too, with an upgraded sensor and more battery life, but it's the Viper I'm interested in. The Viper V4 Pro is already plenty light at 49 g, but the carbon fibre one is said to be even lighter at 47 g. This is the opposite of what I expected, given that the carbon fibre version of the Corsair Sabre V2 Pro is heavier than the regular one . But hey, I'll take it.
Except actually, maybe I won't take it, because Kami also says the mouse is "currently listed in some markets at roughly $300 USD." This matches what Chinese tech news site Expreview relays , at least if currency conversion rates are relevant. According to the site, (login-walled) JD.com has it listed for 1,999 Chinese Yuan (RMB), which converts to $299 USD.
This price tag is especially hard to stomach given the regular Viper V4 Pro is the cheapest of the newest premium, big-brand gaming mice. It's still expensive at $160, but that's cheaper than the $180 X2 Superstrike , $200 X3 Superstrike , and $180 Rival Pro /Sensei Pro.
Razer is going carbon fibre 👀• Viper V4 Pro: 47g• DeathAdder V4 Pro: 49g, upgraded Focus Pro 50K Gen-3 sensor and longer battery life.Currently listed in some markets at roughly $300 USD. https://t.co/D5NjxePv0S October 13, 2026
It's quite nice that the absolute best gaming mouse on the market is cheaper than its other premium competition. It will not be nice if we see another version of it going for almost 2x the price and costing much more than these other expensive mice. People are still rightly reeling a bit at $200 price tags for gaming mice, so $300 will not be a pretty sight.
Hopefully it's just a different market/currency conversion issue. At any rate, none of this is confirmed, so let's just keep our eyes peeled.

title: 'AI godfather' worries we're creating 'alien beings' with artificial intelligence, with pesky moral implications
text:
Geoffrey Hinton is a computer scientist known for his foundational work in AI, specifically when it comes to neural networks (ie, approaching machine-learning a bit like our fleshy brain-learning). As such, he's been described as the 'AI godfather'. But, perhaps surprisingly, he recently described AI as "alien beings" that humans have a "moral obligation" towards.
"We’re creating alien beings—meaning we’re not the only intelligent beings around," He said in a recent interview with The Guardian , "And the reality is, we only have a couple of years to adapt to that.”
Hinton claims, "AI models understand what they’re saying. You couldn’t possibly answer all the questions without understanding the question. It’s ridiculous to say they don’t understand.”
Now, far be it for me to argue with an expert in the field, but I feel like 'understanding' is doing a lot of heavy lifting here. For just one thing, I'm not sure an 'answer' consisting of what is statistically most likely to follow a prompted question is really 'understanding.' In other words, I don't have a Nobel Prize laureate like Hinton does, but I am at least familiar with the Chinese Room thought experiment .
Hinton also says, "The reality is, we’re making beings of a different kind. And the big tech companies keep saying: we want it smarter. This is crazy. We should care as much about all the other aspects of a being as you do about its intelligence.”
A close up of the vacant expression of Meta's Muse AI mascot, Jolly. (Image credit: Meta) AI regulation and 'alignment' (ie, training AI to have the same goals and values as humans) have been hot button issues lately. For instance, the OpenAI-Hugging Face incident is not yet a small dot in the rearview mirror, and the president of Microsoft claims that a carton of milk is more regulated than AI .
Hinton cut his ties to Google in 2023 in order to "freely speak out about the risks of AI," and he's sceptical about the AI industry's attempts to self-regulate. He quips, "Do we think tobacco companies should have been allowed to design the warnings on the packets? So that they could print them in a six-point font, in dark grey on black?"
Even so, Hinton also expresses concerns about the path to AI regulation, saying that humans bear a moral obligation towards AI models.
"Once you start talking about, ‘We have a moral obligation towards these alien beings,’ you lose your audience. I’ve struggled with this issue," Hinton says, "We care about people. [But] we’re making these things and there’s nothing to stop us giving these things—which are more intelligent than us—less rights than us. I’m willing to be selfish and choose human beings. Of course, we should try to make them so that they’re very happy in a symbiotic relationship with us, where our concerns are weighed more heavily than their concerns."
The face of a robot in Atomic Heart. (Image credit: Mundfish) Hinton argues, “People have a very bad model of what people are, and that’s why they fail to understand how these AI models are very like us. Most people don’t understand what consciousness is. They don’t understand what subjective experience is, and they’re very confident that even though they don’t understand it, they’re sure AI doesn’t have it.”
While I'm not a doctor of Philosophy myself, I do know someone who is—our very own Jacob Fox. He's already shared his thoughts on the subject of 'AI consciousness' here , and I asked him for his insight again on this story.
The face of an AI in Prove You're Human. (Image credit: Sunset Visitor) Jacob told me he did not agree with Hinton's moral obligation argument, going on to write more broadly, "While it's good that Hinton is acknowledging subjective experience is relevant to consciousness, he hasn't given a single good reason why we should take seriously the idea that AI has it. And when we interpret personhood as to do with objective characteristics such as rationality, behaviour, and so on, rather than experience, we run the risk of ascribing moral and legal and political weight to them. Which runs the risk of giving AI companies a massive moral argument to keep the industry going, despite how it affects actual humans."
To put it another way, the industry argument for AI consciousness or AI rights is not an altruistic one—it is arguably a cynical tactic to continue business as usual.

title: Hogwarts Legacy's DLSS 5 update shows devs have been listening to PC gamers about keeping it the hell away from game characters
text:
The promised new DLSS 5 model is set to launch in a matter of days, alongside the new RTX Spark chip powering a bunch of new and expensive laptops . As we hoped and expected, the new model shrinks down the overall footprint and therefore the performance overhead, too. But that's not the only issue that's seemingly been fixed.
Nvidia's own stats, which we'll be able to verify soon enough, state that it has half the GPU hit the September version launched with, and offers up a reduction in 4K VRAM usage of 20% as another little statty tidbit. Nvidia says it has done this by refining the training data and reducing the model size down to around 118 million parameters; roughly 24% smaller.
Which is great, because once the feature had released—in NBA2K27 and subsequently pretty much any other game you could think of —the biggest issue we've had with it is the significant performance hit you get just from enabling the feature. Originally Nvidia told us that they expected around a 60% performance hit from turning it on in NBA2K27, and that is now going to be just 30%.
I've spent a long time playing around with DLSS 5, in mods and the official games, and I've been enjoying it. Sometimes the performance hit isn't worth the upgrade, but with that gap closing it looks like it will get there.
This is a different model, and from talking to developers at a recent Nvidia event, you would be able to see some differences were you to put them cheek-by-jowl. Yet those differences should be subtle enough that the performance improvement will still be the main thing you takeaway from the experience.
Considering it's pretty light-touch stuff in NBA2K27—especially when you're spending most of your time zoomed out, taking in just the top third of the court—30% is a far more acceptable performance drop compared to losing over half your frame rate.
(Image credit: Nvidia) The other big issue we had with DLSS 5 was obviously what it was shown to do to character models in the initial reveal back in March this year. The most obvious example was the yassified Grace, who became the unwanted poster child of DLSS 5. And it's been quite telling that none of the games that were revealed back then, including Resident Evil Requiem, have released DLSS 5 updates to their games.
Until now.
Yes, finally Hogwarts Legacy is getting its DLSS 5 glow up . But it's very clear from the side-by-side shots that Nvidia is now presenting on its blog about the new update that the developers have been affected by the negative publicity the feature got on its announcement.
Warner Bros. Warner Bros. Looking at the new images and the effect seems to be almost entirely one of environmental lighting and materials. Pull the before/after slider across the images with characters in and you'll see their features charge not one iota. Compare that with the initial Hogwarts reveal and the difference is night and day. Or DLSS on or off, if you will.
The devs have clearly pulled those sliders back a whole lot, if not masked off the character faces entirely.
Whether this will encourage more gamers to take a look at DLSS 5 I don't know, but I've encouraged even the nay-sayers to at least check out the mods to see what the feature does. Yet we know PC Gamer readers are yet to be convinced; we ran a poll about a month ago to see if readers had tried it, but 65% of readers who responded to the question of whether they had tried DLSS 5 said they were just not interested. With a further 17% waiting on further official releases such as these.
The new update is coming on November 5 if you want to see the world of Hogwarts Legacy getting some finer ambience. What doesn't yet have a date is the only other official game to get a Neural Rendering update: Where Winds Meet. The action RPG will get confirmed support "in the near future" and it's a similar situation to Hogwarts where the only real impact of DLSS 5's update is on the environment. It looks great, but clearly the devs are once more swerving serving up an AI beauty filter for its characters.
We'll get you some of our own numbers on the new DLSS 5 model very soon.

title: 韩国最大短剧平台「Vigloo」登上App Store娱乐免费榜Top2！再次将韩国短剧市场的“卷”推到了新高度！
text:
据七麦数据监测，10 月 11 日，「 Vigloo 」在韩国 App Store 娱乐免费榜排名升至 Top2、并在应用免费榜升至 Top5。并且该 App 已连续多日保持在娱乐免费榜高位，截至 10 月 14 日，其仍占据韩国 App Store 娱乐免费榜 Top2。 作为韩国音频社交巨头 Spoon Radio 于 2024 年推出的短剧 App，「Vigloo」目前已成为韩国本土最大的短剧平台。 据 DataEye 发布的 2026 年 8 月全球短剧应用收入榜里，「Vigloo」双端收入约 530 万美元，环比增幅超 130%，排在第 11 位。
「Vigloo」在韩国 App Store 娱乐免费榜排名升至 Top2
七麦数据观察到，该 App 于 2024 年 6 月 30 日上线 App Store，其主打竖屏短剧，单集时长通常为1—2分钟。其韩国区 App Store 商店产品页面介绍，产品覆盖多元题材，采用免费试看 + 会员解锁的观看模式。
七麦数据监测显示，2026 年 9 月 1 日至 10 月 10 日期间，「Vigloo」在韩国 App Store 娱乐免费榜最高从第 48 位攀升至第 2 位； 截至 10 月 14 日 13 时，该 App 仍在韩国 App Store 娱乐免费榜占据 Top2。
「Vigloo」在韩国 App Store 免费榜排名趋势
同时，据七麦数据监测， 10月14日在韩国 App Store 娱乐免费榜Top10中，短剧平台多达5款 ，可以说是卷出了新高度！
10月14日，韩国 App Store 娱乐免费榜Top10
随着韩国微短剧产业的快速发展，本土平台也逐渐向全球市场布局。2024年第一季度，「Vigloo」成为首家在日本制作原创短剧内容的韩国平台，延续了 Spoon Labs 海外市场（占其总销售额60%以上）的成功基因。据DataEye统计2026年8月收入约42%来自韩国、约40%来自美国。
“本地原创”标签仍需验证真实吸引力
作为韩国短剧出海的重要代表，「Vigloo」的“本土原创”做得非常明显，其并不是简单把韩国内容翻译出海，而是针对不同市场定制内容。 比如，针对当地观众定制本地化作品，建立本土合作制片方等等。但是我们也发现一个现象，虽然美国、日本等市场是其海外收入的主要来源，但与韩国市场相比，它在这两个地区的榜单表现仍然相对平缓，上升空间很大。除去广告投放等动作外，原因之一可能在“本土原创”。下面我们以日本市场为例，来看看能发现哪些问题并获得哪些启示。
据媒体报道，Spoonlabs 日本团队早在 2025 年 6 月对外公告，推出三部日本原创短剧作品，其中包含 松川星 主演的日韩合拍剧集；同时也安排了日本官方 X 账号的选剧投票与转发活动。可以看到，这里已经有本地演员、具体剧目，以及面向当地用户的传播入口。
2026 年 6 月，公司再次官宣，将 「Vigloo」 编剧孵化项目 「Vigloo」 Writers’ Room 第二期招募范围，从韩国拓展至日韩两国，计划招募 28 名编剧，并且为日本创作者配备日语翻译与本土工作人员进行指导。可以看出企业有意持续扩充日本本地创作产能。
对短剧增长团队来说，最核心的推广策略之一是：“本地原创” 这个标签，但是如何真正打动用户，吸引用户点开剧集、持续观看呢？其实仅仅打上 “本地制作” 标签，并不能保证用户看懂剧情冲突，更无法保证用户看完第一集之后继续追更。 与“本土原创”相比更值得我们思考的是：哪一类本地内容，能真正被当地用户接受。
另外，本土演员、贴近当地生活的职场、家庭故事，都可以作为广告素材的测试方向。已经同时布局多市场的短剧团队，可以尝试先在同一个市场、同一部剧上，准备两套广告素材，一组主打本土演员、本地场景，另一组主打剧情悬念。尽量保持投放渠道、目标人群、出价、投放时段一致，商店产品页面和剧集落地入口都指向同一部短剧。这样才能分清，用户点击广告，是被地域本土化标签吸引，还是被故事剧情本身打动。
结语
通过「Vigloo」这款产品我们可以看到， 评估本地化策略，最好按照“市场 × 剧目 × 卖点”的维度拆分，不能只看支持的语种、原创内容的数量。 延续上述的素材对照测试思路，团队可以通过埋点观察用户点击后的剧集开播率、首集完播率、后续剧集解锁行为；同时核算新增用户带来的收入，以及获客、内容制作、本地化的综合成本。如果主打本土演员的素材能拉高点击量，却无法带来有效的剧集观看，建议检查广告素材承诺和正片首集内容是否匹配；当观看数据、收益回收同步达标后，再尝试扩大这类本土化素材的投放规模。
后续我们也可以持续观察「Vigloo」新剧目上线后，哪些具体卖点能在各自的市场留住用户。对于资源有限的短剧团队，建议先把一部剧的下载转化逻辑验证清楚，或许会比直接复制全套本土原创制作方案，更容易落地。

title: 10万买个皮肤，玩家用钱给腾讯国民IP新游“投了票”
text:
前不久，一个消息引发了 游戏日报 的关注，在《王者万象棋》中一款编号为“888”的棋盘染色皮肤，被以近十万元人民币的价格拍下。
虽说事件相对极端，但大额付费一定程度上反映出《王者万象棋》成功立下了“认同感”：大家觉得它是个值得投入的游戏。这和此前外界的“主流”看法有些偏差。
作为“王世界”后王者IP的第二款新品，《王者万象棋》自9月上线便承载着更为严苛的审视，比如即便取得了和《王者荣耀》会师iOS畅销榜TOP5的成绩。 在 游戏日报 报道的评论区，也仍能看到许多网友认为是王者托举带来的短期用户量所致（打万象棋，王者会送限时点券）。
时至今日，《王者万象棋》已上线一个月有余，《王者荣耀》内相关活动也已结束，跳出外部因素后，这款游戏可以说已经走向了自我循环的验证阶段。
这时候再来看《王者万象棋》还能不能立得住？为找到答案，游戏日报与多位自走棋品类玩家、攻略创作者、收集氪佬聊了聊。从他们的讲述中，《王者万象棋》的吸引力逐渐清晰开来，也让我们理解了“10万”是怎么来的。
留下来的理由，不只是"王者"
“凡桥”在游戏行业做过几年，玩过的自走棋不算少。他大学时会在课堂上开金铲铲，后来也玩了王者模拟战，《王者万象棋》上线后第一时间就下载体验。
但他聊起为什么留下来，没说什么高深的理论，只说了一句：“我只要想起来就会打一把。”原因很简单：轻量化。
《王者万象棋》正式上线前，《王者荣耀》内部先上线了“迷你战”作为精简预热版，包体极小，甚至不到30MB。凡桥就是先体验了迷你战，确认有趣才下载了正式版。迷你战每局几分钟就能打完，上手门槛比完整版低很多，本质上是《王者万象棋》“轻量化”理念的一次低风险测试。
正式版的轻量化并非内容少，而是把传统自走棋里最耗精力、最劝退新手的几个痛点解决了。
正式版的轻量化并非内容少，而是把传统自走棋里最耗精力、最劝退新手的几个痛点解决了。首先在时间上，《王者万象棋》单局稳定控制在15分钟以内，6人局10分钟一局，开局成本低。在规则方面，游戏取消了利息和连胜连败奖惩，每回合收益固定，玩家不用再精打细算经济循环。
其次，《王者万象棋》在操作方面对战斗阶段全自动进行，玩家只需完成升级、购买等操作，对局有AI助手基于选角和阵容做操作引导，进一步降低了操作负担，让不熟悉自走棋的玩家也能快速上手。
另外，玩法理解上，《王者万象棋》取消了“三连升星”和复杂羁绊，改成‘单英雄升级’，单局内等级上限999，等级越高伤害越高。
“新手只需要知道高等级棋子厉害、低等级棋子弱就可以了。”自走棋品类核心玩家“明晓已晚”提起《王者万象棋》的等级设计时不由得说到。
作为《王者万象棋》攻略创作者，最开始游玩时明晓已晚还觉得这个等级系统不够直观，体验后迅速理解等级带来的战力差异性，也很快体会到这种设计的好处，新手能更快理解游戏目标。
从这四点看，《王者万象棋》的轻量化，是给传统自走棋“学习成本高、操作负担重、单局时间长”的三座大山凿了一条隧道。这种轻量化快节奏，正是其切入自走棋市场的补位点。
但轻量化只是让人愿意打开游戏。真正让人一局接一局打下去的，是爽感。“一刷、二养、三炸场”，这句官方宣传语恰是《王者万象棋》重爽感的最佳总结，而和玩家聊下来，游戏日报发现游戏爽感还不止于此。
凡桥形容第一种爽感是“猛猛往里面打牌”：“玩过《杀戮尖塔》的人，如果经历过一回合打出20张牌，就能理解这种感觉。”
因为《王者万象棋》没有利息机制，每回合都在出牌、升级、让队伍成型，不会出现某些回合必须等待收益最大化而拖慢节奏的情况，爽感是连续的。
同样是多年自走棋品类玩家的“凉月”对第二种爽感的理解更具体——操作性。他喜欢频繁地刷牌、递牌，看着某个英雄或者整个阵容的等级一路往上跳。等级涨上去的那一刻，满足感就来了，“每天都忍不住刷个几局”。
《王者万象棋》中不少棋手技能和效果牌所需的操作频率，远高于传统自走棋。以棋手白歌＋三分倒转玩法的组合为例，角色卡牌每次登场触发联动效果，就会提升其他角色的等级，同时为棋手技能充能，棋手充能完成后又反哺角色卡牌等级，形成循环。
这种频繁操作并非负担，而是正反馈的来源——每操作一次，等级就涨一点，棋子就强一分。
在对局里，棋子等级高的爽感以最直接的画面表现呈现。当高等级棋子打出终结技时，屏幕震动、满屏特效、击杀敌方棋子时出现酷炫表情包、终结对局时展示酷炫动画都在说明《王者万象棋》把“赢了”从冰冷的数值和结算界面，变成了被无限放大的感官冲击，而为了继续追求这种冲击，玩家也会不断寻找更多的阵容可能性。
明晓已晚说到这种满屏特效疯狂升级的爽感时提到了他喜爱的钻石狂潮玩法，这个模式节奏更快，阵容等级提升更高，视觉表现更加炸裂，是《王者万象棋》爽感在玩法层面的极致体现。
钻石狂潮需要使用游戏内的钻石货币参与，游玩时卡组购买和拍卖都需要使用钻石，所有玩家花费的钻石会积攒进奖池，并受事件效果影响，最终按游戏排名分配。
“星瞳”因为钻石狂潮燃起更高游玩热情，最入迷的时候一天连打六个小时，睡不着的时候就会开一把。她用一句话概括这个玩法的吸引力：“用更少的钱打更多的收益。”
排名不决定盈亏，投入和产出之间的不确定性，让每一局都像在博弈。她用一句话来形容：“有的时候你稳操胜券，看后来者为了名次疯狂争夺，这种鹬蚌相争渔翁得利的感觉也很爽。”
结合两位玩家的讲述，我了解到这种博弈性的根源：钻石是游戏中比较珍贵的货币，不能直接用现金获取，只能通过游戏内行为获取。在高回报的诱惑与落空的代价之间，这种高风险高回报的玩法会给玩家带来刺激感，心率直线飙升。
四种爽感叠在一起，对应的是不同玩家的不同需求。但它们的共同效果是一样的：让人忍不住再开一局。
玩家“买单”的理由，不只是好看
《王者万象棋》不是一款Pay to Win的游戏，各类皮肤道具都无法提供直接的战斗力加成。那玩家在为什么付费？几位玩家的回答，不约而同都先提到了美术。
凉月用“都市时尚潮玩风”来形容《王者万象棋》的美术风格。
王者英雄们被重塑成类似泡泡玛特手办的形象，搭配镭射银为视觉信号的场景设计，UI整洁干净，没有弹窗或红点提示。凉月认为这种现代风的冷调霓虹和金属质感抓住了他的眼球，相较于其他自走棋游戏，他表示还是更喜欢《王者万象棋》的画风。
明晓已晚购买了棋手闹闹的“蓝瘦”皮肤并充值月卡，理由是：“一方面，美术真的很好看，另一方面我会对长期使用的棋手产生一种别样的情感进行消费。”
几位玩家的回答都在说明，《王者万象棋》的美术具有强烈的辨识度和鲜明的审美主张，为它消费的玩家，买的是对这套审美的认同。
而长期游玩下与角色产生的羁绊，是另一个消费驱动力。当你长时间使用一个棋手，他就不再是一个功能单位，而是一个有情感连接的对象。
还有一类玩家，付费是为了收藏和稀缺性。凉月就是典型。他有“全收集”强迫症，皮肤、头像框、聊天气泡、成就、卡面都不能错过。
他提到的这些收集元素，是属于《王者万象棋》的可收集非属性类道具。例如可升级的角色卡牌、多种类别的成就等；至于棋盘、头像框这类常规网游外观收集品，游戏里也量大管饱。
这些收集品的获取和升级大多绕不开刚刚提到的钻石，通过活动、成绩、玩法收集的钻石最终会流向卡面升级、交易行购买等收集行为。这套游戏内货币自循环系统并不刻意刺激玩家充值，但给愿意投入的人提供了足够深的收集池。
凉月也参与过编号888、999的棋盘拍卖，两场编号的个人出价均为十万点券（约一万人民币），远低于成交价。他认为开服编号更稀有、游戏人气也不错、顺子号有收藏价值。所以心理价位在两三万人民币。
但后续拍卖的涨幅让他改变了主意：他感觉这场拍卖已经偏离了收藏的范畴，大家都盯着这个皮肤赌气式加价。竞拍将要结束时，棋盘价格突然上涨了不少，其中一位竞拍者私信他协商棋盘拍卖归属，那一刻他意识到，这场拍卖已经和收藏无关，于是理智地选择了退出。
他也坦言：“竞拍那一瞬间参加者是会上头的。在游戏内的拍卖环节，十几块钱买一张牌的情况也经常出现，大部分时候肯定是溢价的。”
凉月的经历恰好说明《王者万象棋》没有设置付费门槛或付费诱导机制，而是让玩家们为对游戏的认同、并肩作战的羁绊和收藏的稀缺性买单。
结语
说到底，《王者万象棋》这一个月就回答了一个问题：抛去王者IP的外壳，它自己究竟好不好玩。
答案写在数据里：连续11天霸榜iOS免费榜，畅销榜最高冲到第5；开服20天，100万玩家打上了最强王者。就连那个编号888的棋盘，也是被玩家真金白银拍到百万点券的。每一项数据背后，都是玩家用行动写下的答案。
在问到“还会在《王者万象棋》玩多久？”时，四位受访者都明确表示会继续玩下去，“万象棋”和“玩下去”，念起来读音相似。对于一款上线才一个月的游戏来说，这或许是一个巧合，但希望它不只是一个巧合。

title: 讲谈社怀旧恐怖ADV《1999TOKOYO Building》11.10发售！试玩版现已发布！
text:
新式怀旧×恐怖冒险游戏《1999TOKOYO Building》确定于2026年11月10日（周二）发售。本作预定由讲谈社Game Creators’ Lab通过Steam平台推出。
在正式发售之前，自今日起试玩版将会免费上线Steam。试玩版完整收录第一章，玩家可以尽情体验约两小时的游戏内容。游戏内音乐由曾负责《折言》原声音乐的中岛康博担任。
此外，本作还确定由Animate推出原创周边商品。部分正在制作中的周边设计将与今日发表一道提前公开。
Steam商店页面：https://store.steampowered.com/app/4099810/
※本作包含部分暴力、冲击性表现，以及与自杀有关的描写。
■游走于禁忌的探索与命悬一线的对话交锋
右：不想被别人知道的事情，每个人总有那么一两件吧？
本作是一款恐怖冒险游戏。玩家需要潜入房间，调查那些古怪而又危险的同事们的“秘密”，目标是在不被杀死的情况下，与他们平静地共同生活。游戏由两种环节交替推进：一种是在低多边形风格绘制的360°背景中，通过点击调查展开探索（入室盗窃）；另一种则是与Live2D角色互动，展开选项驱动型的视觉小说对话。
故事舞台设定在1999年12月的“常夜大厦”，这是一所破败的室内游乐园，传闻有人在这里“人间蒸发”般地消失了。失去记忆、误入常夜大厦的主人公灯良，
在入室盗窃时被老板夜野撞见，于是被迫留在常夜大厦，成为一名住在园内的员工。然而，与他共同生活的同事尽是一些危险人物。一旦惹恼了他们，谁知道会有什么下场。
利用自己擅长的开锁技巧潜入他们的私人房间，找出他们的“秘密”，并寻找能够让自己活下去的线索吧。
左：员工之间似乎也并不是很和睦……
右：如果不了解对方就无从得知什么事情会触怒他。然而，知道得太多反而也可能引起对方的怀疑…
在对话环节中，对方的反应会根据玩家的选项发生变化。哪怕只是稍微惹对方不高兴，也有可能立刻死亡。在Live2D技术的加持下，角色在对话过程中能无缝切换各种表情。
了解同事们的秘密也就意味着会触碰到他们各自的烦恼与痛苦。在这场与死亡如影随形的奇妙交流中，灯良究竟能否逃离常夜大厦？
【登场角色】
昼行 灯良｜失忆少年
本作主人公。因入室盗窃被老板撞见，他以包吃包住为交换条件过上了在常夜大厦打白工的生活。拥有能够打开任何锁的高超技术。
卡梅莉亚｜总是一副臭脸的占卜师
在占卜馆担任占卜师的少女。兴趣是制作人偶。性格急躁。
鲛岛｜自卑的水槽饲养员
独自负责管理环绕常夜大厦的巨大水槽。大胃王。
伯爵｜自称超人气魅力反派
深受女性顾客欢迎的表演者。总是打扮成德古拉伯爵的模样，不过经常翘掉演出。
常夜侠｜热血特技演员
他是在英雄秀中与伯爵战斗的“常夜侠”。在常夜大厦的居民之中意外地算是比较正常的人。
寿 祝｜神经质的员工
认真负责的员工。与老板夜野一起撑起了常夜大厦的运营事务。
夜野 一人｜工作狂经理
常夜大厦的老板。在这个动不动就人手不足的室内游乐园里，每天24小时不间断工作。
■完整收录第一章的试玩版将于今日发布
第一章的关键人物是伯爵与卡梅莉亚。猜疑、恐惧、背德感，以及友情。本作独有的魅力全都汇聚其中。
《1999TOKOYO Building》试玩版今日起正式在Steam平台免费发布。试玩版完整收录第一章约2小时的大容量游戏内容，玩家既可以与常夜大厦的居民们进行交流，也可以非法入侵他们的房间来探求他们隐藏的秘密。
Steam商店页面：https://store.steampowered.com/app/4099810/
游戏内音乐由曾负责《折言》音乐的中岛康博担任。除了能令人回想起1999年时代气息的怀旧曲风之外，音乐还会随着主人公心境的变化，在不中断播放的情况下自然改变曲调。敬请玩家关注这种紧贴剧情发展的全新音乐体验。
中岛康博（X：https://x.com/looppark）
作曲家。在大阪艺术大学影像学科就读期间，自学了影视作品的作曲方法。曾在电视节目制作公司工作，后于2014年独立。参与电视广告等广告影像、动画、音乐剧的作曲、编曲及音效制作。在游戏领域，曾负责《折言》的原声音乐。
■确定将由Animate推出原创周边
本作确定将由Animate推出原创周边商品！此次将提前公开其中一部分商品的设计。
完整商品阵容、价格以及发售时间等详细信息，将于日后另行公布。敬请关注讲谈社游戏实验室官方X帐号（X：https://x.com/kodanshaGCL）并耐心等待。
■由在常夜大厦打工的兼职店员运营的官方社交媒体账号也在发布最新情报！
欢迎大家关注！
TOKOYO Building🌙（X：https://x.com/1999tokoyo）
■创作者简介
常夜不动产（X：https://x.com/TOKOYO_FUDOSAN）
由剧本作家永濑满月、插画师兼Live2D建模师荻野新月，以及游戏设计师兼工程师凑葵组成的三人游戏制作团队。2024年6月，在成为GCLA Fellow之后入选讲谈社Game Creators‘ Lab。本作是该团队的出道作品。
■商品信息
游戏名：1999TOKOYO Building
平台：Steam
Steam商店页面：https://store.steampowered.com/app/4099810/
支持语言：日语、英语、简体中文
类型：新式怀旧×恐怖冒险
发售日期：2026年11月10日（周二）
试玩版：现已发布（收录第一章，游玩时间约2小时）
游玩人数：1人
开发者：常夜不动产（X：https://x.com/TOKOYO_FUDOSAN）
音乐：中岛康博
发行商：株式会社讲谈社
版权标识：©常夜不动产／讲谈社
■关于讲谈社Creators‘ Lab
讲谈社Creators‘ Lab（https://creatorslab.kodansha.co.jp/）是株式会社讲谈社第四事业本部于2021年6月成立的研发部门。
以“重新定义编辑”为理念，与各种类型的创作者建立联系，推出产品的形式不拘泥于书籍、杂志等。
・负责支持独立游戏创作者并策划新游戏开发的“讲谈社游戏实验室”
・运营匹配型漫画投稿网站DAYS NEO等服务的“用户生成内容媒体实验室”
・负责支持独立影像创作者以及开展全新影像企划的“讲谈社电影实验室”
・不限定领域、广泛支持创作者成长与进阶的“创作者助力实验室”
・针对企业及地方政府面临的问题，提出利用内容力量解决方案的“内容设计实验室”
・Creators‘ Lab由以制作人思维打造全新内容的“IP企划实验室”等部门构成，在助力创作者实现梦想的同时，也运用“编辑”的力量，为企业及地方政府解决各类课题。
有关“讲谈社游戏实验室”的最新信息，请查看以下官方网站及X账号。
官方网站：https://creatorslab.kodansha.co.jp/game/

title: Roblox Expands Live Creator Tournament Series to Brazil
text:
Last April, eight Roblox creators battled for the Champion’s Crown and $50,000 across some of the platform’s top competitive games. Tomorrow, our third annual Creator Showdown—and our first-ever international esports showdown—will be streaming live from São Paulo, Brazil. Eight Brazilian creators in teams of two will compete in five popular Roblox games for the crown and the first place prize of $50,000 Brazilian reais. But every team will take home something, with additional prizes of R$25,000, R$15,000, and R$10,000, respectively, for the second- through fourth-place teams.
The Creator Showdown livestream will begin at 5 pm BRT (1 pm PDT) in Portuguese on Roblox’s Brazilian YouTube and TikTok channels—and in English on our official YouTube , Twitch , and TikTok channels.
In Brazil, popular Brazilian creators LimaMosca , MoonyCaroll , and Ana Xisdê will co-host the livestream. Actor and dancer LimaMosca is well known in Brazil’s gaming community for content around popular titles such as DOORS, Dandy’s World, and Animal Hospital. He’s served as an official host and caster for Roblox events across Latin America for the past several years. A talented dancer, actor, and creator, MoonyCaroll is known for her vibrant personality, signature blue hair, and undeniable charisma. She made her first appearance as a caster at Gamescom last year and has made a name for herself in the gaming community. Internationally recognized, Ana Xisdê has transformed her passion for gaming into an award-winning professional career. From the countryside of São Paulo to some of the world’s biggest stages, she brings the passion, experience, and expertise she’s gained in the gaming industry.
For English speakers, the livestream will be co-hosted by popular Brazilian YouTube streamer Febatista and WaffleTrades , a streamer known for his content around Roblox events, avatar items, and giveaways.
The full lineup includes four teams:
Lucas Clash ON and Canal Clash War
Nayu and iBugou
Teodoro and Godenot
NatashaPanda and Vick Barbosa
The Brazil Creator Showdown will require teams to compete in five games:
Showdown: Anime FPS Jutsu Shooter : An anime-style first-person shooter featuring precision gunplay and jutsu (special abilities). Teams will compete in an esports arena built directly into the game’s Shibuya-inspired hub.
Clean Crew : A multiplayer roguelite survival horror game featuring cooperative gameplay, enemies, and bosses that spawn unexpectedly. Players must partner up to clean abandoned apartments while avoiding hazards and fighting off pests.
FIFA Super Soccer : Official FIFA-partnered soccer game featuring fast-paced gameplay and customization. Teams will need to use advanced dribbling and passing skills to take the win.
Beat Battles : Competitive music creation and remixing featuring stage battles, voting, and special audio effects. Players will compete to drop the best beat by creating original music using a custom piano roll or remixing unique audio loops to create tracks.
Killstreak Battle Royale : A fast-paced arcade first-person shooter and battle royale featuring fluid movement, tactical gunplay, and consecutive elimination rewards. Players parachute onto a map and have to work together to locate gear and weapons, survive a shrinking zone, and fight to be the last team standing.
We’re excited to bring the Creator Showdown to São Paulo and celebrate the imagination that Brazilian creators and players bring to these games in this live elimination tournament.
